prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 2D merge · Clinic schedule (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Time" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Monday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Tuesday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Cardiology clinic (Dr. I" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Dermatology" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Staff training — closed " spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Time" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 49px
  col 2: header "Monday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 419px
  col 3: header "Monday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 97px · one-line width 97px
  col 4: header "Tuesday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 109px · one-line width 109px
  col 5: header "Tuesday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 99px · one-line width 406px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 682px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 681px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 682px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Show the clinic schedule by time, day and room, including shared closures and activities that span time slots.","reading":"Readers scan down the time column, then across the Monday and Tuesday room columns to locate or compare activities. Merged cells show when an activity covers multiple times or rooms.","groups":["Monday Room A and Room B belong under the Monday header; Tuesday Room A and Room B belong under Tuesday.","All four room columns play the same scheduling role and should remain easy to compare.","The time column identifies each row and can be narrower than the activity columns."],"keep_intact":["Time labels such as 09:00 and 10:00","Room identifiers and day names","Names, abbreviations and individual words where the available width permits"],"may_wrap":["Long clinic descriptions at word boundaries","The staff training closure across its merged cell","Activities spanning two time slots can use the combined row height for wrapped text"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[70,153,153,153,152],"idea":"Give the four room columns nearly equal width to make comparisons across days and rooms straightforward."},{"name":"B","widths":[70,185,125,130,174],"idea":"Give more space to Monday Room A and Tuesday Room B, which have the longest one-line content, while retaining readable widths for the other rooms."},{"name":"C","widths":[70,135,125,160,194],"idea":"Favor the Tuesday columns, especially Room B, while allowing Monday Room A’s long description to wrap into the height of its two-row merged cell."}]}
